records.sourceAnchor: NIDHI-TBI official page: startup route, host route, beneficiaries and periodic TBI calls
observations: NIDHI-TBI supports technology and knowledge-driven incubation infrastructure and services. The official page says startups apply directly to a TBI and receive support after that TBI accepts the application.

The detailed guideline is primarily an institution route: eligible academic/technical/R&D or other proven institutions, a not-for-profit society/trust/Section 8 entity, adequate expertise and infrastructure, and generally three years of institutional existence subject to the stated government-entity exception.

The guideline requires a transparent incubatee-selection system, an agreement with incubatees, defined residency/exit terms, facilities and performance monitoring. It is not a direct cash grant to every startup that reads the programme page.

The NIDHI page says TBIs periodically announce startup calls, while the current NIDHI homepage showed no generic open-call post when checked. A startup-facing match therefore requires a specific TBI and live local call.
reviewFollowUps: Replace the discovery-only primary source in the seed record with the official NIDHI-TBI page/guideline before publication, while retaining Startup India as cross-check evidence.
Verify the current TBI list, local calls, admission criteria, fees/equity terms, residency, exit policy and services for each matched startup.
Keep host-institution grant support separate from startup incubation access.

records.sourceAnchor: NIDHI-CoE official page: five-year institutional support, startup incubation access and periodic CoE calls
observations: NIDHI-CoE strengthens existing TBIs into higher-capability incubation centres with design, product, prototype, validation, patent and technology-incubation facilities.
The guideline describes enhanced institutional support of up to INR 50 crore over five years; this is an establishment/strengthening support ceiling for the CoE, not a direct startup entitlement.
Startups and innovators may apply for incubation support to a CoE, but each CoE periodically announces its own enrollment call, selection criteria, services and terms.

The official page states that nine CoEs have been supported and provides a list route. The current generic NIDHI homepage did not show an open generic call, so current startup-facing availability must be checked per CoE.
reviewFollowUps: Verify the current CoE list, each centre's focus, live enrollment call and application route.
Extract institutional grant conditions, milestones, infrastructure ownership, reporting, sustainability and recovery terms from the current guideline and sanction documents.
Present startup access as incubation/acceleration support, not as the INR 50 crore institutional figure.

records.sourceAnchor: NIDHI-EIR official page: INR 10,000-30,000 monthly, maximum 12 months, selected TBI route
observations: NIDHI-EIR is a fellowship for students, researchers, innovators and entrepreneurs pursuing a technology business idea; it is not a startup loan, investment or unrestricted company grant.

The current official page states financial support from INR 10,000 to INR 30,000 per month for a maximum of 12 months, together with TBI infrastructure, mentoring, technical/financial advice and industry connections.

The April 2022 guideline permits a 12-month period to be extended up to 18 months only for deserving candidates and with selection-committee approval. The extension must not be presented as automatic.

Applicants apply through selected NIDHI-EIR centres/TBIs, and the current centre call, education/experience requirements, full-time commitment, concurrent-support restrictions, ownership disclosures and local selection terms must be confirmed.
reviewFollowUps: Verify the current selected-centre list, local call, application form and any amended fellowship terms.
Keep monthly fellowship, TBI services and any conditional extension as separate benefit buckets.
Do not show the monthly amount as total startup funding or imply guaranteed selection.

records.sourceAnchor: NIDHI-SSP official page: incubator grant, startup support cap and periodic incubator calls
observations: NIDHI-SSP is a two-level route: DST provides grant-in-aid to eligible incubators, and the incubator then provides seed support to selected incubatee startups. These are not the same benefit.
The official page states up to INR 1000 lakh for an incubator and up to INR 100 lakh for a deserving startup. The startup cap is not an automatic award or a direct DST payment to every applicant.

The guideline requires an eligible Indian company, preferably DPIIT registered/applied, at least three months' association with the incubator, customer/USP clarity and at least 51% Indian promoter shareholding under the stated conditions.

The instrument may be soft loan, equity or equity-linked; agreements must define milestones, repayment/recovery, equity liquidation and monitoring. Funding can therefore create repayment or ownership consequences.
Startup applications are made to listed incubators/TBIs through their periodic calls. No generic national startup deadline was treated as verified from the official page.
reviewFollowUps: Verify the current seed-supported TBI list, each incubator's call, instrument, valuation/equity, repayment, milestone and due-diligence terms.
Separate the incubator-level grant from the startup-level investment/soft-loan/equity support in the data model and UI.
Confirm current guideline version and any amendments before using the INR 100 lakh startup cap in recommendations.

records.sourceAnchor: DST NQM startup-support guideline, pages 1-6: eligibility, application modes, selection, funding/equity, milestones, mentoring, monitoring and Government support
observations: The guideline supports DPIIT-registered Indian startups with market-fit, scalable and commercializable quantum-technology products or services, subject to Indian-company, India-based IP, ownership and promoter-shareholding conditions.

The startup route is mediated by NQM thematic hubs. The official DST startup page lists computing, communication, sensing/metrology and materials/devices routes and instructs a startup to apply to only one hub.

Track 1 describes seed funding up to INR 5 crore with incubation equity, while Track 2 describes equity or CCPS up to INR 25 crore for startups with prior VC funding. These are guideline reference structures, not automatic entitlements; milestone tranches and agreements apply.
The guideline also describes mentoring, facilities, user-agency engagement, demo days and possible Government procurement preference, subject to the applicable hub route and current terms.

The historical I-HUB QTF call and any hub page do not establish a current universal deadline. Current hub windows, route-specific terms, valuation, dilution, milestones, monitoring, facility charges and grievance routes remain unresolved.
reviewFollowUps: Verify the current open call, intake window, application form and vertical fit for each linked NQM hub.
Confirm the current hub legal structure, funding instrument, equity/CCPS, valuation, dilution, milestone and incubation terms against the latest guideline or agreement.
Confirm the latest guideline amendments, procurement preference, facility, monitoring and grievance conditions before publication.
Keep mission outlay and fund-level figures separate from startup-level benefits and never present them as an applicant entitlement.

publicationGuard.reason: NIDHI-TBI, CoE, EIR and SSP are incubator-mediated or institution-led routes with different applicants, instruments, local calls and indirect startup benefits. Official sources support structured drafts, but current centre-level availability and detailed terms require human review before publication.
